## Guesty and Hospitable - A Fair Overview Before the Head-to-Head


Most vacation rental property managers and operations leads assume the real decision is simply about picking the right PMS or channel manager, that whichever of Guesty or Hospitable has better automation features will handle the messaging load and let the team focus on higher-value work. That assumption is understandable after doing the demos, reading the review sites, and still feeling like something is missing. That feeling is accurate.


Both platforms have earned their reputations honestly, but they were built for different operators at different stages, and conflating them costs more than just time. Neither platform fully solves the problem that sits underneath the PMS decision: how guest communications actually get handled, at volume, across channels, without letting a slow reply or a missed message quietly damage your review scores.


### Guesty at a Glance - Enterprise-Grade PMS Built for Portfolio-Scale Operations


Founded in 2013, Guesty has[raised over $409 million in](https://getlatka.com/companies/guesty) total funding, with[estimated ARR reaching $163.7 million](https://getlatka.com/companies/guesty) in 2024, up from $100 million the prior year. **Guesty is genuinely built for professional property managers** running 20-plus properties who need enterprise-grade infrastructure and are prepared to negotiate pricing that reflects it.


That last point deserves more than a footnote. The pricing model is a genuine friction point for operators below enterprise scale: each new feature unlock tends to carry an additional cost, and the cumulative effect is a bill that surprises managers who expected an all-in-one platform to behave like one. For operators pushed onto the full Guesty platform after relying on a lower-cost entry tier, the transition can feel forced and expensive rather than earned by growth.


Managers running fewer than 100 properties routinely discover that Guesty's infrastructure was never sized for them, and that realisation usually arrives after the contract is signed. The operational consequence matters here: when pricing friction drives operators to stitch together workarounds, guest communication is usually the first thing that suffers. Response times slip.


Issues escalate into negative reviews that could have been resolved in the first exchange. Protecting review scores means responding fast and resolving issues before they escalate, a standard that manual workflows and patched-together tooling consistently fail to meet at any meaningful volume. AI becomes operationally relevant: its AI Agents are most beneficial when a business receives a high volume of repetitive guest messages and already has documentation, SOPs, FAQs, and property manuals to train the agent on, with the first automated guest reply going live days after connecting those materials.


Conduit's integrations are built specifically so that businesses already using tools like Notion, Google Drive, or Airbnb can point the agent at existing content without manual re-entry, meaning there is no second system of record to maintain.


### Hospitable at a Glance - Automation Built for Independent Hosts


Hospitable started life as Smartbnb, an automated messaging tool for independent hosts, and that origin still shapes what it does best: clean interface, accessible onboarding, predictable per-listing pricing, and solid rule-based automation. On Capterra and G2, Hospitable consistently earns highly positive ratings based on verified user reviews aggregated on those platforms. The honest caveat is that it was architected for hosts managing one to twenty properties, and some enterprise-facing features feel bolted on rather than built in, a pattern visible in reviews where users at the 15-plus property threshold specifically cite gaps in owner reporting and API flexibility.


Hospitable's rule-based messaging works well for predictable touchpoints: check-in instructions, checkout reminders, post-stay review requests, and multi-platform inboxes that need monitoring simultaneously. That gap is exactly where an AI-powered inbox and workflow layer adds the most.


Conduit's Workflows trigger after events in the guest lifecycle, a booking confirmed, a check-in completed, a specific keyword detected, replacing the manual staff action that otherwise falls through the cracks. The Inbox is designed for operations and support teams that need to monitor and manage all conversations the AI agent is handling across multiple platforms or properties simultaneously, without toggling between dashboards.


### What Happened to Guesty for Hosts and Why It Changes the Competitive Landscape


Guesty consolidated its entry-level product, formerly known as Your Porter, into its main platform, ending the lower-cost tier that served smaller hosts. This consolidation clarifies the competitive lines: Guesty is now unambiguously targeting professional managers. For the operators who were caught in that migration, hosts who built workflows around a more accessible price point and were pushed to a product priced for portfolios ten times larger, the experience reinforced a broader lesson: the platform layer and the communication layer are separate problems, and solving one does not solve the other. The PMS holds your reservations. The question of who responds to the guest at 11 p.m., how fast, and whether the answer protects your rating or costs you one, that is a different system entirely.


> *"Guesty's pricing model feels costly and opaque, every new feature requires an additional unlock fee, leaving me feeling nickel-and-dimed and pushing me to look at alternatives like Hospitable."*


## Guesty vs Hospitable Feature Comparison - What Each Platform Actually Delivers


Counting features is the wrong[unit of analysis](https://atlasti.com/research-hub/unit-of-analysis) . The more useful question is which features actually move the needle for your specific portfolio size, and on that measure, the gap between Guesty and Hospitable is narrower than the marketing suggests on most dimensions, and decisive on a few that matter enormously to professional operators.


### The Feature-by-Feature Table


Feature Guesty Hospitable Decisive for…


Channel integrations 50+ OTAs Core OTAs (Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com) Operators needing broad distribution beyond the top three


Unified inbox Multi-property, multi-channel Multi-property, core channels Both adequate for sub-50 portfolios


Automation rules Deep trigger logic,[conditional branching](https://support.higherlogic.com/hc/en-us/articles/360033052971-Conditional-Branching-and-Skip-Logic) Solid messaging sequences; narrower trigger set Operators building complex, multi-step workflows


Direct booking Custom domain, configurable branding, ties to accounting Simple setup, limited branding controls Operators actively reducing OTA dependency

Trust accounting Native, full-featured Absent Professional PMs handling owner funds


Open API Fully open; broad third-party marketplace Zapier-reliant for most custom connections Operators connecting specialized tools


According to industry research, Guesty connects to over 50 OTA and distribution channels while Hospitable focuses on a curated set centered on the top three. The channel breadth gap becomes decisive only when a portfolio's revenue strategy requires Expedia, niche platforms, or direct API connections to regional OTAs.


### Direct Bookings, Integrations, and Where Each Platform Draws the Line


Hospitable's direct booking site is easy to activate. The trade-off is configurability: branding controls are limited, and the product is not designed to serve as a primary direct channel for operators serious about reducing OTA commission dependency. Guesty's Booking Engine supports custom domains, deeper branding controls, and native integration with its trust accounting and owner reporting stack, the stronger choice for operators who treat direct bookings as a revenue strategy rather than a nice-to-have.


The honest caveat: **Guesty's configurability creates setup complexity** . Operators without a dedicated ops resource may find the flexibility more burden than benefit, a friction point that is real and underacknowledged in Guesty's own positioning, even as its own documentation walks new users through the scope of what switching entails. On integrations, Guesty's open API and third-party marketplace spans revenue management, dynamic pricing, guest experience, and accounting tools.


Hospitable relies on Zapier for most custom connections. If your operations depend on a specialized pricing tool or custom reporting layer, Guesty's ecosystem gives you the connection points. **More integrations also mean more configuration, more sync points to monitor, and more places for data to drift.** Operators who don't need the extensibility are paying for complexity they'll never use.


### The Feature Both Platforms Treat as an Afterthought


Industry analysis notes that operators managing 20 or more properties are most likely to extract full value from Guesty's feature set. Trust accounting, configurable owner reporting, and open API access are genuine differentiators for professional PMs with owner accountability obligations. But this surfaces an architectural paradox that neither platform's marketing acknowledges directly: **Guesty's enterprise feature depth, its 50+ OTA connections, open API, and configurable direct booking engine, is precisely what makes its guest communication layer proportionally less capable of handling the message volume those same features generate.**


More channels mean more inbound guest messages. More properties mean more simultaneous conversations. And the operators we work with who run multi-property portfolios consistently describe the same breaking point: their teams end up switching between platforms constantly, drafting messages in one tool, checking guest history in another, tracking sentiment in a Google Sheet that no one fully trusts.


Resolution times stretch. Shift handoffs become a liability. Managers lose reliable visibility into whether guests are actually satisfied or just quiet.


One operator's customer experience team saw guest resolution times stretch significantly under that fragmented setup, with sentiment tracked manually and handoffs requiring agents to read entire conversation histories from scratch. The same pattern surfaces on the staffing side. Operators who have built virtual assistant teams to handle guest communications find those teams consumed by the mundane, Wi-Fi codes, parking instructions, check-in logistics, while higher-value work goes untouched.


The result is that the operator, despite having SOPs in place, gets pulled back into daily operations as the de facto communication manager. This is where the PMS-native messaging layer, no matter how capable on paper, reaches its structural limit. It is built to route and log messages, not to resolve them intelligently at scale across time zones, properties, and channels simultaneously.


An AI communication layer trained on your existing SOPs and manuals, and connected to your inbox so the operations team can monitor every conversation the agent handles, addresses the volume problem the PMS was never designed to solve. That means the AI agent is most effective precisely when the business already has documentation to train on, receives a high volume of repetitive guest messages, and uses tools like Notion, Google Drive, or Airbnb where existing content can be leveraged without manual re-entry. The PMS handles the operational record.


The AI handles the conversation. The gap neither Guesty nor Hospitable closes is not a feature gap. It is a response-quality-at-scale gap, and it widens in direct proportion to how many channels and properties a platform like Guesty helps you add.

## Guesty vs Hospitable Pricing - What You'll Actually Pay as Your Portfolio Grows


Subscription fees are the first number operators write down when comparing Guesty and Hospitable. They are rarely the last number that matters. The real cost only becomes visible when you account for what sits underneath the monthly invoice: onboarding, add-ons, support tiers, and staffing hours that grow with every new property.


### Guesty's Pricing - Not on the Website


Guesty does not publish a public price sheet. Its model is percentage-of-revenue or a custom enterprise contract, meaning the only way to know your actual cost is to book a sales call. Across the market, operators running 5 to 50 units land in undisclosed tiers that require direct negotiation.


The pattern is consistent: Guesty carries the reputation of enterprise power at an enterprise price, a real affordability concern for operators whose portfolios are still growing. Smaller property managers in particular often find themselves effectively priced out as they scale past a certain threshold, absorbing costs that were never visible on a pricing page. The final number is negotiable only if you know to push.


Operators who skip that negotiation often pay significantly more than peers running similar portfolio sizes.


### Hospitable's Per-Listing Subscription - Predictable Until It Isn't


Hospitable charges a flat per-listing monthly fee, which makes budgeting straightforward at five properties. Stress-test that math at 35 properties and the picture shifts. Operators managing 20-plus listings frequently find the total subscription crossing a threshold where Guesty's percentage model, if negotiated well, becomes competitive. Neither model is obviously cheaper at scale; the answer depends entirely on booking volume and willingness to negotiate.


### The Onboarding Fee Nobody Budgets For


Guesty carries a large onboarding fee that does not appear on any public pricing page, flagged consistently as a significant surprise cost on top of the recurring platform fee. This one-time charge can quietly erase months of perceived savings before the platform is even live. Hospitable's onboarding is lighter, a genuine structural advantage for smaller operators who want to move without a five-figure entry cost.


### The Line Item Both Pricing Pages Omit - Guest Communication Labor


This is the cost that neither platform mentions, and it is often the largest one. Guesty and Hospitable automate workflows and route messages. They do not resolve them.


What most teams report is that property managers spend a substantial share of team hours each month on routine guest communication alone, a burden that scales with every listing added. A 35-property portfolio is not a 5-property operation with seven times the software cost; it is seven times the message volume landing in an inbox that still requires a human to clear it. That staffing reality is exactly where operators hit a ceiling the software pricing models never account for: scaling the portfolio without proportionally scaling the headcount required to manage it.


Every new listing adds repetitive pre-arrival questions, check-in instructions, mid-stay requests, and post-stay follow-ups, the kind of high-volume, predictable guest touchpoints that currently require a staff member to action manually, and that Conduit is built to absorb. Its AI Agents are trained directly on a property manager's existing SOPs, FAQs, and manuals, with no manual re-entry required if those documents already live in tools like Notion, Google Drive, or Airbnb, via native integrations.


Once connected, the agent begins handling guest messages automatically, typically delivering the first automated guest reply within days of setup. From that point, the agent runs continuously, before, during, and after every stay, responding the moment a guest or customer sends a message, across every platform simultaneously. The Inbox gives the operations or support team a single place to monitor, review, and oversee every conversation the AI agent is handling, so coverage does not require someone to be on-call around the clock.


Workflows layer on top to handle recurring, predictable guest lifecycle moments, booking confirmations, check-in sequences, keyword-triggered responses, automatically, after the trigger event fires, without a staff member initiating them. The practical result: an operator managing 35 properties can handle the guest communication load of that portfolio without the headcount structure of a 35-property operation. The goal is not to replace the team; it is to get off the 24/7 on-call treadmill and back to growing the business, scaling coordination capacity without scaling the payroll line that sits invisibly beneath every Guesty or Hospitable invoice comparison.

## Who Each Platform Is Best For: and Where Both Hit a Wall


Both platforms serve short-term rental operators, but they are not competing for the same operator. Where you sit on the portfolio scale, and what you actually need the software to do at that scale, determines which one fits and which one starts working against you.


### Guesty's True Sweet Spot - Professional Managers Running 20+ Properties


Guesty is built for operators who run property management as a business. Its enterprise tier targets portfolios at the 20-plus property threshold, where you need trust accounting, owner statements, a configurable open API, and multi-channel distribution across dozens of active listings. The reporting depth alone justifies the cost at that scale. If you are managing properties on behalf of owners, fielding investor questions, and coordinating an operations team, Guesty gives you the infrastructure to look like the professional you are.


### Hospitable's True Sweet Spot - Independent Hosts and Small Operators Who Want Clean Automation


Hospitable earns its reputation at the one-to-fifteen property range. Setup is approachable, per-listing pricing is predictable, and the automation rules cover the standard guest journey cleanly. An independent host who wants booking confirmations, check-in instructions, and review requests to go out without manual effort gets that without a dedicated ops hire. The trade-off is real: as your portfolio pushes past fifteen to twenty properties, the feature ceiling becomes visible. Operators who have been there describe a specific moment where the tool starts feeling built for a smaller version of their business.


### The Portfolio Scale Where Each Platform Starts to Strain


The strain point differs for each platform, one is financial, the other functional:


Platform Strain Type What Breaks Down


Guesty Financial before functional Pricing is custom and negotiable, but community consensus is consistent: the cost is significant, and smaller operators frequently find themselves paying for enterprise modules they do not use


Hospitable Functional before financial The per-listing model stays affordable, but automation logic does not deepen proportionally with portfolio size


### The Structural Blind Spot Both Platforms Share - Rule-Based Triggers Are Not Guest Intelligence


Both Guesty and Hospitable automate message scheduling. A booking confirmation goes out. A check-in reminder fires at T-minus 24 hours. A review request triggers on checkout. That is scheduling, not intelligence. The moment a guest sends something outside the predefined trigger set, "Can we store luggage an hour early?" / "The hot tub is making a noise", the automation stops and a human has to respond.

At 35 properties, off-script message volume becomes a staffing equation, not an automation one.

A Verdict on Guesty vs Hospitable, Plus the Layer Both Miss

The real verdict is not which platform wins outright; it is understanding that your PMS decision and your guest communication strategy are two separate choices. ### The Clear Verdict - Which Platform Wins for Your Portfolio Size and Complexity


**Portfolio size is the cleanest decision filter.** Guesty fits professional property managers running 20 or more properties who need enterprise-grade trust accounting, open API flexibility, and deep OTA integrations. Hospitable fits independent hosts and smaller operators (roughly 1 to 20 properties) who want clean automation, predictable per-listing pricing, and a faster setup curve. The mistake is choosing Guesty at five properties because it sounds more serious, or stretching Hospitable past the point where its integration limits start showing.


### The Guest Communication Gap Guesty and Hospitable Leave Open


Both platforms automate scheduling, channel sync, and rule-based message triggers. What neither does is deploy an AI agent that reads your SOPs and autonomously resolves the many messages per booking that arrive outside business hours, across every listing, every night. Industry analysis consistently identifies[communication overhead as a primary cost](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9709815/) lever for operators managing larger portfolios, one that scales with headcount rather than software licenses. Operators who discover this gap after signing up for either platform report the same outcome: they hire a VA, then another, then a night-shift coordinator. The PMS did not cause the problem, but it did not solve it either.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What's the real difference between Guesty and Hospitable?


Guesty is built for professional property managers running 20-plus properties who need enterprise-grade infrastructure, trust accounting, open API access, 50+ OTA integrations, and configurable owner reporting. Hospitable started as an automated messaging tool for independent hosts and remains best suited for operators managing one to twenty properties, with a cleaner interface, predictable per-listing pricing, and solid rule-based messaging automation, but gaps in owner reporting and API flexibility that surface around the 15-plus property threshold.


### Does Hospitable handle guest messaging automatically?


Hospitable's rule-based messaging handles predictable touchpoints well, check-in instructions, checkout reminders, and post-stay review requests. Where it strains is under genuine conversation volume: guests who ask questions outside the rule set, edge-case requests that arrive at 2 a.m., and multi-platform inboxes that need simultaneous monitoring. That gap is where a purpose-built AI communication layer trained on your SOPs and property manuals becomes operationally relevant.


### How much does Guesty actually cost?


Guesty does not publish a public price sheet, the only way to know your actual cost is to book a sales call, since its model is percentage-of-revenue or a custom enterprise contract. The pattern across the market is consistent: Guesty carries an enterprise price, and operators who skip negotiation often pay significantly more than peers running similar portfolio sizes. Add-ons, onboarding fees, and support tiers add to the final number in ways that are not visible on any pricing page.


### Which platform is better for scaling beyond 30 properties?


Neither platform fully solves the operational problem that surfaces at scale. Guesty's enterprise feature depth, 50+ OTA connections, open API, configurable direct booking, generates proportionally more inbound guest messages, yet its communication layer was never architected to resolve them intelligently at volume. Operators running multi-property portfolios consistently describe the same breaking point: switching between tools, tracking sentiment manually, and watching resolution times stretch as shift handoffs become a liability. An AI communication layer trained on your existing SOPs and connected to your inbox addresses the volume problem the PMS was never designed to solve.


### Can Hospitable or Guesty handle automation across complex, multi-step workflows?


Guesty supports deeper trigger logic and conditional branching, making it the stronger choice for operators building complex, multi-step automation rules. Hospitable offers solid messaging sequences but works with a narrower trigger set. That said, both platforms treat guest communication as a feature rather than a core operational problem, neither was built to read your SOPs, interpret nuanced guest questions, or resolve conversations intelligently at scale across time zones and channels simultaneously.
